editorial_intent: Diagram how dense negatively charged sulfate groups on neuronal heparan sulfate proteoglycans electrostatically trap positively charged patches of alpha-synuclein fibrils, physically blocking their bulk glymphatic clearance through the interstitial matrix.
subject: A cross-sectional micro-architectural breakdown of neuronal membrane carbohydrates: heavy, rigid thread-like alpha-synuclein protein aggregates are anchored to negatively charged sulfate nodes on extracellular sugar chains, contrasting with an open, un-sulfated channel on the right where smooth fluid vector arcs flush unbound protein fibrils into cerebrospinal drainage channels.
setting: Framed by a geometric cranial meridian dome with a subtle 24-division circadian astrolabe calibration arc and phase-coherent geodesic neural constellation rendered in precise Bauhaus linework.
composition: Post-Constructivist dual-panel lithograph layout on unbleached archival paper; the left side demonstrates electrostatic entrapment within a dense matrix grid, while the right side transitions into a dynamic linear vector flow representing uninhibited glymphatic fluid clearance.
